largest_vegas_favorite.note: Largest Vegas favorite this week (-550 ML, ~85% raw implied) — by policy we don't crown a pick on raw favorite status alone. It went through the same Advocate/Skeptic/Arbiter debate as everyone else (see its entry below) and still ranks #1 post-debate, but the recommendation goes to the next-best team instead.

process_note: Each shortlisted team's case was built by an Advocate (live research), stress-tested by an independent Skeptic subagent looking only for flaws, and resolved by an independent Arbiter subagent that weighed both sides without seeing the raw research trail. Teams outside the top-10 shortlist got a lighter single-pass positives/negatives note instead of the full three-stage debate.

board.summary: The Advocate's case is essentially structural — Arizona benched its franchise QB for a game-manager backup, which is close to a fatal roster decision for Week 1. The Skeptic's injury notes are real but describe players still expected to suit up; the line movement (11.5 → 9.5-10.5 despite lopsided public money) is the one point with teeth, trimming the edge slightly without erasing it.
positives: -550 ML (~85% raw implied) at home in a dome
Arizona benched franchise QB Kyler Murray for backup Jacoby Brissett
negatives: Justin Herbert nursing a plantar fasciitis issue from camp (mobility/timing risk)
EDGE Tuipulotu (hip) and LT Slater (recovering from patellar tendon tear, 'flare-up' in pads) both banged up
Spread has fallen 11.5 → 9.5-10.5 despite ~79% of money on LAC — sharp money/books less convinced than the raw line suggests
Arizona retains real skill talent (Marvin Harrison Jr., James Conner); Brissett is low-ceiling but not turnover-prone
trap_flags: reverse line movement — spread fell from 11.5 to 9.5-10.5 despite ~79% of public money on LAC, suggesting sharp/book skepticism

board.summary: The Skeptic's strongest thread (Verse addition, unknown new DC) mostly restates general Week 1 uncertainty rather than specifically favoring Cleveland, and 'trap game' chatter is narrative, not evidence. The core fact — a declining Deshaun Watson leading a rebuilding team with a new HC/DC on the road — still dominates, so the Advocate's number holds with only a minor discount.
positives: -455 ML (~82% raw implied) at home
Cleveland in a full rebuild under new HC Todd Monken, having just traded away Myles Garrett
Deshaun Watson fully healthy but in visible decline
negatives: Cleveland got a quality DL piece (Jared Verse) back in the Garrett trade; new DC Mike Rutenberg is a total unknown
JAX's own HC publicly said he has 'no idea' what Cleveland will run defensively
Local coverage openly debating this as a trap game after a surprise 13-4 season raised expectations
Actual line (-8.5) is a field goal shy of what an 82% ML would typically imply — market hedging more than the raw number suggests
trap_flags: post-breakout trap-game narrative (surprise 13-4 season raising expectations)
new-system uncertainty (Cleveland has a brand-new, unproven DC)

board.summary: The Skeptic lands a real blow here: two starting safeties on PUP and the starting CB released is a specific, verifiable, high-impact weakness — not vague pessimism — and it's exactly the kind of hole a hot-closing Saints passing attack could exploit. Combined with a 49.5 total signaling a competitive script, the safe-floor case is meaningfully weaker than the raw -334 ML suggests.
positives: -334 ML / -6.5 at home
Jared Goff healthy, one of the league's better offenses
negatives: Both starting safeties (Kerby Joseph, Brian Branch) opened on PUP; starting CB Terrion Arnold was released — secondary genuinely depleted
Lost both coordinators after 2024 (Ben Johnson to CHI, Aaron Glenn to NYJ); replacements only in year two
Saints closed 2025 hot and are veteran/division-tested despite being battered
49.5 total prices in a shootout, not a blowout

board.summary: Solid home favorite, but discounted from a pure power-rating gap because Jayden Daniels is making his first start back from a serious elbow injury and both squads are breaking in new offensive coordinators — real variance the spread doesn't fully price in. Note: this team wasn't part of this round's formal three-stage debate (a board-generation gap caught after the fact) — treat as slightly less rigorously vetted than the other top entries and worth re-running through the full process next time.
positives: Big home favorite (-5.5) over Washington
Coming off a strong prior season at home
negatives: Jayden Daniels making his first start back from a serious elbow injury — unpredictable variable
Both teams installing new offensive systems under first-year coordinators — added game-flow uncertainty
Washington missing starting LT Laremy Tunsil (torn triceps)

board.summary: Losing Tua for Rush does help Pittsburgh, but the Skeptic correctly notes Rush is a credible spot-starter, not a total liability, and pairs that with specific concerns (Rodgers' history of slow openers, reported camp absences, PIT's documented struggles closing out lesser teams). The line already reflects a competitive game; the debate nudges this down slightly.
positives: -4.5/-5.5 at home
Falcons' planned starter Tua Tagovailoa is out (oblique) — Cooper Rush makes his first start for Atlanta
negatives: Cooper Rush is a veteran with real spot-starting experience, not a total unknown
Atlanta still has Bijan Robinson, Drake London, Kyle Pitts
Aaron Rodgers (42) has a real history of slow season-opening starts
Multiple Steelers reportedly missed camp/preseason time; PIT's offense was middling in 2025

board.summary: Lamar Jackson and an upgraded defense still make Baltimore the better team on paper, and that carries real weight even on the road. But Daniel Jones being fully rested off a healed Achilles (vs. the hobbled version fans saw late in 2025), plus Indianapolis's actual 8-2 start last year, is a legitimate counter that trims the edge to near a true toss-up-plus.
positives: 3.5-point favorite even on the road
Lamar Jackson-led offense and an upgraded defense
negatives: Daniel Jones returns fully rested from a Week 14 Achilles tear — could be more dangerous healthy
Indianapolis started 2025 at 8-2 before its second-half collapse — early-season form has been strong before
Lamar Jackson missed four 2025 games to hamstring/back injuries; recent fragility is real even if 'cleared' now

board.summary: The Skeptic's rebuttal is the sharpest on the board: the 'two first-round picks' were compensation for trading away a 52.5-sack perennial All-Pro (Micah Parsons), meaning this defense is actively weaker, not stronger — and the 11-1 series history is essentially noise from entirely different rosters. Harbaugh is a legitimate program-builder, not a placeholder. This is close to a coin flip with real bust risk.
positives: -162 ML road favorites
11-1 in the last 12 series openers vs. NYG
negatives: The added draft capital was compensation for trading away Micah Parsons — defense is rebuilding around rookies, not stacking strength
John Harbaugh is a proven program-builder, not a green first-timer, and has hyped Jaxson Dart
11-1 series trend compiled under entirely different rosters/staffs — weak evidence
48.5 total implies a track meet, not a defensive stranglehold

board.summary: The Advocate's edge is thin to begin with (62% implied), and Carolina isn't the team that started 2025 poorly — a Bryce Young with real late-season/playoff success, at home, against a first-time road HC, is a legitimately live upset spot. Some books already show a tighter number than the posted ML implies.
positives: -164 ML road favorites (~62% implied)
Oddsmakers project a 24-21 Bears win
negatives: Bryce Young improved markedly down the stretch in 2025 (23 TD) and beat the Rams in the playoffs — real momentum
True road game; Ben Johnson's first regular-season game as an NFL HC on the road
Some books have Carolina as short as +3, tighter than the ML implies
Caleb Williams still had real late-season turnover/pressure issues in 2025

board.summary: The Skeptic surfaces a concrete schematic mismatch (LV's 32nd-ranked run defense vs. a top-13 Achane-led ground game) that directly undercuts the 'established home favorite' framing — both teams are actually in new-HC uncertainty, since Kubiak is himself a rookie HC. Willis's low-mistake profile paired with a strong run game supports a competitive script.
positives: -3.5 favorites at home
Miami turning to Malik Willis as full-time starter
negatives: LV's run defense finished 32nd (dead last) in 2025 vs. a top-13 Achane-led Miami ground game
Both teams are in brand-new HC eras — Kubiak is himself a rookie NFL head coach
Willis has a low-mistake college-backup track record (3 TD/0 INT in two seasons) paired with a strong run game

board.summary: Both sides largely agree this is a near-toss-up, and the Skeptic doesn't add much beyond what the Advocate already priced in — Burrow's own health uncertainty was implicit in a 52-57% model split. This settles almost exactly where the Advocate had it.
positives: Favored by 3.5 at home behind Joe Burrow
negatives: Burrow himself returning from a toe injury that cost him nine games in 2025

board.summary: This is the Skeptic's best-supported case on the entire slate: Denver is a defending AFC finalist with an elite, specific defensive profile and a real offensive upgrade (Waddle), while Mahomes returns from a season-ending ACL/LCL injury for his first live game in nine months against exactly that defense. KC's own -144 price is already the thinnest home-favorite line on the board, corroborating rather than contradicting the Skeptic.
positives: -144 ML (~59% implied) hosting Denver on Monday Night Football
negatives: Denver made the 2025 AFC Championship with an elite defense (283.4 yds/game allowed, league-leading sacks) and added Jaylen Waddle
Patrick Mahomes returning from a torn ACL/LCL — first live game in 9 months, on national TV, vs. that defense
-144 is the thinnest home-favorite price on the entire slate — near coin-flip signal
Multiple outlets picking Denver outright

board.summary: The mirror image of KC's entry: Denver's defensive profile and Mahomes' major-injury return make this a genuine toss-up rather than a Chiefs formality, but the road environment and Kansas City's pedigree keep Denver from being a clean favorite either — not a survivor play in either direction this week.

trap_game_policy_note: Trap-game status is capped at the 1-2 most credible upset risks per week (LAC, JAX this week), not a flag for every minor concern. Any trap-flagged team is automatically excluded from the recommendation, same as the largest Vegas favorite — both LAC (largest favorite) and JAX (trap game) were excluded here, so the recommendation goes to DET, the highest-probability team left standing.
